title: The characterized first-factor localization isomorphism
statement: Let R,A,B,Aq,D be commutative rings with compatible R-algebra structures and maps A -> Aq, A tensor_R B -> D and Aq tensor_R B -> D as in [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model]. Let Q be an A-module cochain complex, L a base-derived tensor cohomology model of Q tensor-derived_R B, and K such a model of (Aq tensor_A Q) tensor-derived_R B. Let i be an integer. Define u_Q on the underlying R-complex by x |-> 1 tensor x. Let zeta:L.derived -> K.derived be the unique counit-compatible derived-functor isomorphism. Define c_(L,K) as (L.cohomologyIso i).hom followed by H^i(L.derived(u_Q)), H^i(zeta at Aq tensor_A Q), and (K.cohomologyIso i).inv. A D-linear morphism e is characterized when e(1 tensor x)=1 tensor c_(L,K)(x) for every x. Assume S is a submonoid of A and Aq is its localization, and that all maps to D commute with the A, B and Aq maps. Then there exists a D-linear isomorphism D tensor_(A tensor_R B) L.cohomology(i) -> D tensor_(Aq tensor_R B) K.cohomology(i) characterized by this formula. The formula determines the map uniquely.

source.place: Tag 0DJ8, affine localization identity; Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change

proof.text: Construct the first-factor unit and the canonical cohomology map using the unique counit-compatible derived-functor comparison, as before. Apply the cohomology base-change theorem to this unit; its degreewise generator equation is definitional.

Let phi:A tensor_R B -> Aq tensor_R B be induced by A -> Aq and the identity of B. Tensor induction proves that the composite phi followed by the map to D equals the given A tensor_R B -> D map: on a tensor b, write it as (a tensor 1)(1 tensor b), and use the A, Aq, and B scalar-tower equations.

Apply extension of scalars from Aq tensor_R B to D to the cohomology isomorphism. Compose it with the equality transport for the coefficient maps and ModuleCat.extendScalarsComp. Equality transport preserves 1 tensor x by equality induction; extendScalarsComp sends it to 1 tensor (1 tensor x), and map_tmul followed by the lower generator formula gives exactly IsFirstLocalizationMap. The previously proved hom_ext argument gives uniqueness.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_firstLocalization_iso (S : Submonoid A) [IsLocalization S Aq] (i : ℤ)
    (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (L : ModuleCat.BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A B Q D)
    (K : ModuleCat.BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R Aq B ((extend A Aq).obj Q) D)
    : ∃ e : (ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap (A ⊗[R] B) D)).obj (L.cohomology i) ≅
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap (Aq ⊗[R] B) D)).obj (K.cohomology i),
      IsFirstLocalizationMap R A Aq B D Q L K i e.hom
